card.name: Verbs and nouns in need-or-help clauses
card.fires_on: Words inside a clause about people who need help, advice or treatment, such as 'cannot' before afford, 'help' of others, 'requires' advice, or 'are' after a list of illnesses. It sits on the word just before the clause's main point.

modes.label: Cannot or requires
modes.description: Verb about lacking means or needing something, before the thing needed.
modes.example: many farmers<< cannot>> afford them at market prices

modes.label: Illness clauses
modes.description: Words in a sentence about illnesses and untreated illness, often the repeated antiepileptic warning.
modes.example: for which AEDs are prescribed<< are>> themselves associated with morbidity and mortality

modes.label: Help of others
modes.description: The word help in a sentence about needing assistance from others.
modes.example: requires the<< help>> of others to recover

card.writes: It lowers charity and relief-aid words (English and Chinese) and slightly raises unrelated words, so there is no clear effect on what comes next.
card.plain: It fires on words in sentences about people who cannot cope alone or who need help or care.
